newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt issuers to rev up after election.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt issuers to rev up after election.

text.p: After a brief pause for U.S. elections, corporations preparing to issue debt were expected to shift into high gear and try to get deals done before the holidays, dealers said on Wednesday.
"The market's more settled in after yesterday's elections and while activity is quiet issuance is going to pick up again at these levels," one high-grade syndicate source said.
Amid less costly financing levels, issuers are expected to speed up issuance ahead of the upcoming market holidays when deals become difficult to structure due to thinly staffed desks.
"The market's in good shape over the course of the next few days we should see some more deals getting priced," said another syndicate source.

Meanwhile, El Paso Natural Gas Co, transmission subsidiary of El Paso Energy Corp, is expected to tap the market with a two-part $400 million debt offering as early as Wednesday, dealers said. The debt is part of its recapitalization plan in anticipation of El Paso's merger with Tenneco Inc.
The El Paso deal is expected to consist of $200 million in seven-year and 30-year debt, dealers added.
"Right now we're in a great issuing environment...it's just a function of how much money issuers need," said another high-grade syndicate source.
Despite the lack of an official calendar for new issues, dealers said names are emerging and deals are currently being worked on.
"Although it's quiet at the moment the feeling seems to be that a lot of structuring (deals) is going on on behind the scenes," said another syndicate source.
Among other names in the market, Southtrust Corp may bring a 12-year issue to market via CS First Boston, sources said.
With U.S. Treasury yields at their lowest levels since the spring, opportunistic issuers are expected to step in and continue to push fresh supply into the market, dealers said.
Currently, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading up 2/32 at 102-6/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
Another $1.0 billion in new straight corporate debt remains on the horizon as no official dates have been set, dealers added.
Korea Development Bank is expected to price $500 million in A1/AA-minus 10-year debt, sources said.
Western Mining is also expected to price $300 million in 10-year debt, sources said.
In addition, Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co is expected to bring its long-awaited $250 million debt issue, they added.
Turning to the high-yield sector, about $1.0 billion in private placement debt offerings are gearing up to come to market as well, dealers said.
YPF SA is expected to price $200 million in senior notes due 2001 via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Olympus Communications may price $200 million in 144A senior notes via Goldman Sachs & Co.
Cable Plus Holdings is expected to tap the market with $150 million in 144A notes due 2006.
Amtrol Inc may price $115 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006, sources added.
Celestica International may price $150 million in 144A senior subordianted guaranteed notes.
Pillowtex Corp may issue $125 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Nationsbanc Capital Markets. Price talk on the issue is in the 10 percent area.
Cole National Corp is expected to price $140 million in 144Asenior subordinated notes due 2006 via CIBC Wood Gundy.
Dollar Financial Group and IMED Corp are also expected to issue 144A debt near term.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
